verdict_reason: The output-contract defect is closed and the headline is now the paper's quantity. I settled the question from the arXiv v1 LaTeX source itself (e-print 2401.17139v1, contents/method.tex): the Definition 'Matrix entropy of a dataset' is H(D) = sum_i H(Sigma_{S_i}) / (n log d), and Algorithm 1 line 4 writes H(Sigma_S) = -tr(Sigma log Sigma)/log d -- the log-d divisor is in the paper's own definition and algorithm, not an add-on. The tables report that quantity: appendix table tab:pythia, wikipedia row, gives 0.7938 / 0.7442 / 0.7003 / 0.6580 for 14M/31M/70M/160M, all in [0,1] as H/log d must be. BLME's `matrix_entropy` now returns exactly that, and the kernel is an exact reproduction of the official v1 code: I extracted utils/entropy_dataset.py from the waltonfuture repo's history (commit b1f38b0 -- it is deleted at HEAD) and ran normalize/cal_cov/cal_entropy head-to-head against BLME's _matrix_entropy on five (model, protocol) combinations, max per-document absolute difference 1.05e-06 / 1.28e-05 / 7.05e-06 / 1.87e-06 / 2.08e-05.
comparable_reason: At the SHIPPED configuration the value is rank-ceiling dominated and the ceiling is a width function, and the fix makes this WORSE rather than better because the /log d divisor is itself width-dependent when N << d. I re-measured both halves. (1) Structureless control, iid Gaussian tokens with no model at all: at N=91 tokens (the mean length of the shipped default corpus at max_length=512) the normalised entropy falls monotonically 0.7071 (d=512) -> 0.6684 (768) -> 0.6429 (1024) -> 0.6240 (1280) -> 0.5397 (4096), an artefact range of 0.1674 produced by width alone. At the paper's own N=2048 the same control gives 0.9799 -> 0.8866, range 0.0934, and sits near the top of the scale where it stops binding. (2) Over the 61 archived models (d_model 512-7168) matrix_entropy_normalized has Spearman -0.464 with d_model (p=0.0002), -0.355 with n_layers, -0.171 with vocab and -0.514 with log(params), against an observed range of 0.1584-0.6083 -- so the artefact range 0.167 is over a third of the total spread. The archived RAW headline, by contrast, is uncorrelated with width (+0.042, p=0.75). So the paper-defined normalisation is, at this N, the MORE size-correlated of the two. The metric is comparable only at the paper's N; at the shipped N it is not.

github_reason: Fetched the official v1 kernel from git history -- utils/entropy_dataset.py at commit b1f38b0 of waltonfuture/Diff-eRank; the file no longer exists at HEAD, which now ships only the v2 Diff-eRank kernel. Transcribed it verbatim: normalize() subtracts the token mean then row-L2-normalises; cal_cov() does Z = F.normalize(R, dim=1); A = Z.T @ Z / N; cal_entropy() takes eig = svd(A/trace(A))[1], H = -(eig*log eig).nansum(), and RETURNS H/log(A.shape[0]) -- the official code itself normalises. The driver reads model(id)[0][0,:,:] (the last hidden layer), truncates at max_length=2048, and averages the per-sentence normalised entropies ('alg a'). Head-to-head against BLME on pythia-70m and pythia-160m under three protocols (shipped defaults n=10/L=512; wikitext-103 document-level n=58/L=2048; default corpus n=200/L=2048): max absolute difference per configuration 1.05e-06, 1.28e-05, 7.05e-06, 1.87e-06, 2.08e-05, the residual being BLME's fp32 svdvals against my fp64 reference. Two harmless deliberate deviations: BLME uses svdvals(Z) so the d-N structural zeros never enter the sum, and BLME drops zero-norm rows where the official divides by the raw norm.
paper_reason: Published (v1 appendix, tab:pythia, wikipedia row): pythia-70m 0.7003, pythia-160m 0.6580. Running BLME's kernel at the paper's protocol (last layer, max_length=2048, 58 wikitext-103 document-level articles, mean 1865 tokens) I get 0.812888 (+16.1%) and 0.774007 (+17.6%). At the SHIPPED default (n=10, max_length=512, mean 91 tokens) I get 0.592585 (-15.4%) and 0.550602 (-16.3%). The level is therefore NOT reproduced at either protocol, and the sign of the miss flips with document length -- raw H for pythia-70m runs 3.6967 at 91 tokens, 3.7884 at 119, 5.0711 at 1865 -- so the level is a corpus-length property, not an estimator property. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: the fix note claims 'measured on their protocol: pythia-70m normalised 0.6659 (-4.9%)'. I could not reproduce that at their protocol (I get 0.8129) nor at the shipped default (0.5926); 0.6659 corresponds to raw H = 4.154 at d=512, i.e. an intermediate document length, so it is not a paper-protocol number and should not be quoted as one. What DOES reproduce is the model-to-model delta: published 0.0423, mine 0.0389 at the paper protocol (-8.1% relative) and 0.0420 at the shipped default (-0.7% relative), same sign and same ordering in both. The paper reports its own sampling sd as 0.000349 over 10,000 documents, so a 16% gap is a corpus difference, not estimator noise.
confounds_reason: Re-measured over the 61-model archive with architecture pulled from the local HF configs: matrix_entropy_normalized Spearman -0.464 (d_model, p=0.0002), -0.355 (n_layers), -0.171 (vocab), -0.514 (log params); the archived raw headline +0.042 (p=0.75). The structureless control shows the rank ceiling alone can produce an artefact range of 0.1674 at the shipped N=91 against an observed archived range of 0.450 (0.1584-0.6083), so a real fraction -- but not all -- of the cross-model signal is the ceiling. This resolves substantially at the paper's N=2048 (control range 0.0934, and near the top of the scale), so it is a CONFIG-driven confound and the right fix is to raise N, not to residualise.
defects: CONFIG: the shipped default is num_samples=10 at max_length=512 over a corpus whose documents average 91 gpt2 tokens, against the source protocol's 10,000 documents at 2048 tokens. In that regime N << d and the value is rank-ceiling dominated -- verified on iid Gaussian noise with no model at all, where the ceiling alone spans 0.7071 (d=512) to 0.5397 (d=4096). At this N the number is NOT the Wei et al. number: I measure pythia-70m 0.5926 against a published 0.7003 (-15.4%).

The code's headline is the LAST-layer value (which is what Wei et al. report) and the covariance is formed PER SENTENCE and then averaged. The manuscript matches neither the code's headline nor the paper's protocol.
